sections.title: Morning Coordination
sections.content:
The morning of delivery, confirm the truck is loaded with the correct unit. If your operation allows, verify the serial number matches the order. Check the delivery window with the logistics team — is the truck running on time?

If the team is running late, call the customer BEFORE the window expires. Do not let them wait and wonder. 'Hi [name], the delivery team is running about 30 minutes behind. They will be there by [updated time]. I apologize for the delay.'

sections.title: The Post-Delivery Check-In
sections.content:
The salesperson should check in after the delivery window. 'Hi [name], just checking that everything went smoothly with your delivery today.' This takes 30 seconds and it catches problems while they are small.

If there was an issue, you hear about it from the customer directly — not from a 1-star review three days later.

sections.title: Access Issues
sections.content:
Locked gates, narrow hallways, third-floor walkups, tight elevator access — these are the last-minute surprises that delay deliveries and frustrate everyone.

If you did the pre-delivery communication right, you already know about these. If something unexpected comes up on delivery day, work with the customer and the crew in real time to find a solution. 'Can we take the doors off the hinges temporarily? Can we use the service elevator? Can we reschedule for a time when the building loading dock is available?'
